limitations: Teaching time and glow are schematic; they do not quantify hormones, transport rates, blood flow or biological storage duration.
Exact selectors address aggregate existing parts; this hook cannot identify a single follicular cell or draw an organelle that is absent from the mesh.
The thyroid capillary baskets and arterial/venous trunks are representative disconnected samples. No continuous artery-to-capillary-to-vein tracer route is asserted.
Parathyroid capillaries are a separate representative sample without depicted supply/drainage connections. Thyroid and parathyroid are never one endocrine circuit.
Resorption vacuoles are existing teaching markers associated with colloid scallops, not independently animated objects and not a complete modeled endocytic pathway.
Enlarged cell pitch, basal lamina and parathyroid cells preserve the original teaching layout; molecular callouts have no model-unit size.
Cell height and colloid morphology are activity cues, not sufficient evidence of hormone output or a diagnosis. Geometry never changes during playback.
Pre refine and Post refine require separate runtime instances bound to their independently verified artifact digests. Variant selection belongs to the root application.
thyroid_parathyroid_review_v2 is a distinct frozen model and is deliberately rejected by this hook.

Separate displayed cell rims and narrow teaching clefts do not depict a physiological leak. Follicular epithelium is taught as a sealed polarized barrier; iodide uptake and hormone release cross cells, not display gaps.

steps.title: Closed follicular unit
steps.caption: Polarized follicular epithelium surrounds a colloid lumen; the basal face meets supporting tissue and nearby capillaries.

steps.title: Separate parathyroid context
steps.caption: The original corner sample has its own capsule, chief-cell cords, oxyphil cells, fat and capillary sample.

steps.title: C-cell contextual identity
steps.caption: C cells are distinct from follicular cells and parathyroid chief cells; their product is calcitonin.

steps.title: Basal iodide uptake
steps.caption: Blood supplies iodide; NIS imports it across the blood-facing basolateral follicular-cell membrane. TSH regulates synthesis and release.

steps.title: Apical thyroglobulin supply
steps.caption: Follicular cells synthesize thyroglobulin and secrete it apically into the follicular lumen.

steps.title: Apical iodide delivery
steps.caption: Iodide crosses the apical membrane toward the lumen; no exclusive transporter assignment is implied.

steps.title: Apical iodination
steps.caption: At the apical-colloid boundary, TPO with peroxide iodinates thyroglobulin tyrosines into MIT and DIT.

steps.title: Coupling on thyroglobulin
steps.caption: Coupling on thyroglobulin forms T4 from DIT+DIT and T3 from MIT+DIT.
steps.compartment: apical-lumen boundary; hormone residues remain on thyroglobulin

steps.title: Extracellular colloid storage
steps.caption: Colloid stores hormone-containing thyroglobulin extracellularly; these are bound hormone residues, not a free-hormone pool.
steps.compartment: follicular lumen extracellular to the epithelium

steps.title: Apical colloid retrieval
steps.caption: Apical endocytosis retrieves colloid; the scallop markers identify resorption rather than circulating particles.

steps.title: Lysosomal hormone liberation
steps.caption: Intracellular lysosomal proteolysis liberates T4/T3; lysosomes are explained here without claiming a modeled organelle.
steps.compartment: intracellular lysosomal processing; text-only organelle cue

steps.title: Basal thyroid-hormone release
steps.caption: Free thyroid hormones leave basally toward nearby capillaries; the illustrated trunks do not form a proven route.

steps.title: Low extracellular calcium
steps.caption: Lower ionized calcium means less CaSR activation in parathyroid chief cells, permitting increased PTH secretion.
steps.compartment: chief-cell surface exposed to extracellular fluid

steps.title: PTH into nearby capillaries
steps.caption: Chief cells release PTH toward their own capillaries; this capillary is a separate representative vascular sample.

steps.title: PTH target-organ effects
steps.caption: Off-model targets: renal calcium retention, phosphate excretion, calcitriol production and bone remodeling help restore calcium.
steps.compartment: kidney and bone are described off-model; no physical routes

steps.title: Calcium feedback suppresses PTH
steps.caption: Rising extracellular calcium increases CaSR activation and suppresses PTH release; no dose-response curve is simulated.

steps.title: C cells secrete calcitonin
steps.caption: Elevated calcium can stimulate calcitonin release from thyroid C cells. This does not use colloid storage or iodinated thyroglobulin.

steps.title: Calcitonin physiological scope
steps.caption: Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast-mediated resorption; its normal adult human calcium-homeostasis role is smaller than PTH/vitamin D.
